# zkSPARQL constraint-count evaluation pack

<!-- GENERATED by `bench/zk-compose/scripts/constraint_pack.py` — do NOT hand-edit. Regenerate with `--write`; verify with `--check`. -->

Deterministic circuit-size evidence for the zkSPARQL submission (bead `sq-gum8.5`; design record `research/paper-selection.md` §3.1).

## What this is, and what it is not

Every number below is the `circuit_size` reported by `bb gates -s ultra_honk`, **joined** from the regression-gated snapshot `crates/sparq-zk-compose/tests/gate_count_snapshot.json`. Nothing is hand-typed, the generator needs neither `nargo` nor `bb`, and a re-run is byte-identical.

- **A size, not a time.** No wall-clock figure appears here. Prove/verify timings are machine-dependent; only canonical runs may carry them.
- **A size, not a coverage claim.** What each circuit *proves* is `site/specs/zksparql.typ` §7.1 and `sparql_feature_catalog.json`. The `path_reach` family proves a **bounded-existence** statement — there exists a chain of at most `d` committed triples, `d` public — which is strictly weaker than the SPARQL property path, whatever its gate count.
- **A size, not a security claim.** The estate is internally re-audited but **not externally audited** (open gate `sq-qhy4`); the forge suite is toolchain-gated (`sq-1gir`); the value lane carries the documented INV-VL / CR-G8 downgrade. Nothing here asserts a soundness, privacy, or zero-knowledge property.
- **No third-party figure is reproduced.** See [Related work](#related-work-cited-never-re-measured).

Toolchain baselined for these counts: `bb 5.0.0-nightly.20260324`, `nargo 1.0.0-beta.21` (regression tolerance 3.0%).

## Successful-result circuits (released mapping support)

### `result_v2`

Versioned support for released SELECT DISTINCT mappings with canonical unsigned integer capacity i bits (0 means no private predicate) and status tree depth d. Exact decimal length is private. The small i=8 lane admits values through 99; i=64 covers u64. Preserves issuer authentication and string-commitment binding, without result completeness or holder identity.

## String lane vs value lane

The value lane binds the FILTER operand through the committed value handle of the dual-leaf commitment method instead of hashing a canonical token in circuit. Both sides are joined from the snapshot.

| datatype | string lane | gates | value lane | gates | reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| integer | `filter_int_d2` | 17,416 | `filter_value_dl_int` | 3,033 | 5.7422× |
| double | `filter_f64_d2` | 17,416 | `filter_value_dl_f64` | 4,502 | 3.8685× |
| decimal | `filter_decimal_i3_f2` | 17,416 | `filter_value_dl_decimal` | 3,070 | 5.6730× |

> The dual-leaf host-leaf encoding is **not yet implemented** and the resolver is not wired into `verify_manifest`. This is a circuit-size comparison of two designs, not a claim that the value lane is usable end to end today.

## Related work — cited, never re-measured

This pack reproduces NO figure from any cited system. Constraint counts are not comparable across proof systems, arithmetizations, or circuit granularities: the numbers below are Barretenberg ultra_honk `circuit_size` for WHOLE SPARQL-fragment and credential-layer circuits, whereas the cited works count different objects under different backends (and several report time, not constraints). A ratio between them would not be a measurement of anything, so none is computed. Related work is cited — see site/specs/zksparql.typ section 3 — never re-measured.

| system | domain | proof system | what it reports | figures reproduced here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ZKSQL | SQL over a committed database | interactive, VOLE-based | communication and running time of an interactive protocol | **no** |
| PoneglyphDB | SQL over a committed database | non-interactive, PLONKish | prover/verifier time for whole SQL workloads | **no** |
| ZKGraph | property-graph queries (no RDF/SPARQL surface) | non-interactive, PLONKish | proving cost for graph-query workloads | **no** |
| VeriDKG | SPARQL over decentralised knowledge graphs | authenticated data structure — integrity, NOT hiding | proof size and verification time of an ADS, not circuit gates | **no** |
| ZKLP | IEEE-754 floating-point arithmetic in zero knowledge | lookup-optimised circuits | constraint counts for individual IEEE-754 primitive operations | **no** |

Citations: `site/specs/zksparql.typ` §3 (References).

## Reproduce

```sh
# 1. (only after an intentional circuit change) re-measure the gate counts.
#    Needs nargo + bb; re-baseline the snapshot from the result.
bench/zk-compose/scripts/gate_counts.sh > bench/zk-compose/gate_counts_latest.json

# 2. regenerate this pack from the snapshot (no nargo, no bb, deterministic).
bench/zk-compose/scripts/constraint_pack.py --write

# 3. verify the committed artefacts are byte-identical to a fresh generation.
bench/zk-compose/scripts/constraint_pack.py --check
```

Coverage: 55 of 55 snapshot members across 16 families, 58 single-parameter scaling pairs, 3 invariance facts. The generator **fails** on a snapshot member it cannot classify, so a new circuit family cannot silently drop out of this evaluation.
